issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no obvious puddle, a sweet coolant smell, oil that looks milky or tan on the dipstick, or a slow seep of coolant or oil where the intake meets the engine.
issues.why: The 3.4L V6 uses plastic-framed lower intake gaskets that break down over time and with old coolant. They can leak outside the engine, or inside where coolant mixes with the oil.
issues.next: Check the coolant and oil often. If coolant is disappearing or the oil looks milky, park it and have the gaskets replaced before the bearings or head gaskets are damaged. Fresh coolant afterward is part of the job.

issues.sym: White, sweet-smelling exhaust smoke, coolant loss, overheating, a rough-running engine, or bubbles in the coolant bottle.
issues.why: Head gasket leaks are one of the most reported failures on the 3.4L Rendezvous, often after an intake gasket leak or an overheating episode has gone on too long.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. Ask for a cooling system pressure test and a combustion gas (block) test to confirm it before deciding whether the repair is worth it.

issues.t: Engine overheating and hot warning light
issues.sym: Temperature gauge rising into the red, a hot engine warning on the dash, steam from under the hood, or the heater blowing cold while the engine is hot.
issues.why: Owners report overheating from coolant leaks, a failed thermostat or water pump, or cooling fan trouble. Driving on while hot can warp or crack a cylinder head, which some 2005 owners reported.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off as soon as it overheats. Let it cool, check the coolant level, and have the leak or failed part found before driving again.

issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between gears, harsh or late shifts, a check engine light with transmission codes, or the vehicle losing drive.
issues.why: The 4T65-E automatic in the Rendezvous can wear its valve body and clutches. GM issued bulletins for valve body repairs tied to shift solenoid and pressure codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked. Catching valve body or solenoid faults early can avoid a full rebuild; a slipping transmission usually needs a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Erratic shifting from pressure control solenoid
issues.sym: Shifts that are harsh one moment and soft the next, firm downshifts, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The transmission's pressure control solenoid can wear out and stop holding steady line pressure, which upsets shift quality.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes and pressure checked. Replacing the solenoid is a much smaller job than a rebuild if it is caught early.

issues.sym: A shake or shudder felt as the transmission shifts from first to second, usually at light throttle.
issues.why: GM traced this shudder on the 4T65-E to the second clutch assembly inside the transmission.
issues.next: Mention the GM bulletin for a 4T65-E 1-2 shift shudder to the shop. The fix replaces the second clutch parts, so do not let it go until it slips.

issues.sym: A growl or hum that gets louder with speed and may change when turning; sometimes an ABS light comes on.
issues.why: The sealed front and rear hub bearing units wear out early on many Rendezvous, often around 50,000 to 75,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the hubs checked for play and noise. Replace a bad hub soon, as a failing bearing can also damage the ABS sensor.

issues.sym: The gas gauge reads full or empty no matter how much fuel is in the tank, jumps around, or the low fuel warning comes on early.
issues.why: The fuel level sender inside the tank wears or gets contaminated. GM also issued a bulletin for gauge, hard start and stall problems linked to the sender and fuel pump.
issues.next: Track your mileage and refill early until it is fixed so you do not run dry. The sender is usually replaced together with the fuel pump module.

issues.sym: The speedometer, tachometer, fuel and temperature gauges drop to zero or freeze, sometimes with an odometer error message.
issues.why: Owners report failures of the instrument cluster or of the engine computer (PCM) that sends the gauge data.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Have the module codes read to find which unit has failed. A cluster can often be repaired; a computer must be programmed to the vehicle.

issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm air, or both heat and A/C stop working.
issues.why: Owners report failed A/C compressors and leaks. On some vehicles the climate control unit or blend door actuator fails.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures and leak test done before adding refrigerant. A failed compressor should be replaced with a new receiver-dryer.

issues.t: Water pump and heater pipe coolant leaks
issues.sym: Drips of coolant at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, or the coolant warning coming on.
issues.why: Water pumps and the metal heater supply tubes on the 3.4L V6 corrode or their seals wear out and begin to leak.
issues.next: Find the leak with a pressure test. Fix it soon, since low coolant is what leads to overheating and gasket failures on this engine.

issues.sym: Long cranking, no-start, stalling or loss of power, especially with a low tank.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump wears out, and some owners also found corroded fuel pump wiring at the tank.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested before replacing parts. Check the pump connector and wiring at the same time.

issues.t: Camshaft timing codes on the 3.6L V6
issues.sym: Check engine light with camshaft position codes such as P0008, P0016 or P0017, sometimes with a rough idle.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover camshaft timing codes on this engine, including a crankshaft sensor ring that can move, and rough idle on the 3.6L. Stretched timing chains cause the same codes on GM 3.6L engines.
issues.next: Have a shop read the codes and check camshaft-to-crankshaft timing. Use the oil type GM specifies and change it on time, as oil quality matters for the timing chains.

issues.t: EGR valve codes keep coming back
issues.sym: Check engine light with EGR codes such as P0404 or P1404; the light may come back weeks after a repair.
issues.why: Carbon builds up on the EGR valve so it cannot open and close correctly. GM put out a bulletin for these codes.
issues.next: Have the valve cleaned or replaced and the passages checked. It is not urgent but it can fail an emissions test.

issues.t: AWD warning light and rear drive problems
issues.sym: An AWD disable or service light, a rear drive that does not engage, or noise and vibration from the rear on all-wheel-drive models.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for the AWD disable lamp and for repeat transfer case or transmission failures. Owners also report failed AWD sensors.
issues.next: Have the AWD codes read. Keep tire sizes and wear the same on all four wheels, since mismatched tires stress the system.

issues.sym: A window will not go up or down, falls into the door, or makes a grinding noise.
issues.why: The window regulator or motor wears out.
issues.next: Have the motor and regulator checked. Tape the glass up if it falls so water does not get into the door.

issues.t: Engine may stall or not restart from ignition relay (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may stall, or not restart right away after being shut off.
issues.why: Contamination on the ignition relay contacts raises resistance and can cut power.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for recall 05V-157. The dealer replaces the ignition relay free.

issues.sym: Steering may feel loose or stop responding without warning.
issues.why: The steering column intermediate shaft on some vehicles was too small and could spin inside its coupling.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 03V-052. The dealer inspects and replaces the shaft free.

issues.t: Liftgate could open in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs in normal driving.
issues.why: The liftgate latch support was not strong enough, so the liftgate could open in a severe crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 04V-150. The dealer adds reinforcements near the latch free.

issues.t: Fuel tank check valve can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell around the vehicle, wetness on the side of the tank, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The weld holding the fuel inlet check valve to the tank can crack, letting fuel vapor and drops escape, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 03V-454 and 07V-349. The dealer repairs or replaces the tank free.

issues.sym: No warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator could crack at a weld when it fires, throwing fragments and not fully inflating.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 02V-222. The dealer inspects and replaces the driver airbag module free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may turn on or off wrongly (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light may not match who is in the seat, or an airbag warning may come on.
issues.why: On some vehicles with leather seats, the passenger sensing system can turn the front passenger airbag off when it should be on, or on when it should be off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 06V-417 and have it repaired free. Keep small children in the back seat.
